title: Areas Related to Circles
prerequisites: Formulae for circumference and area of a circle.
Area of a triangle, including the equilateral case.
Understanding of an angle measured in degrees.

topics.title: Sector and Segment of a Circle
topics.quick_summary: A sector is the region between two radii and an arc, and a segment is the region between a chord and an arc; both are found from the central angle as a fraction of 360°.
topics.real_life: A slice of pizza is a sector, and the crust-side piece left after a straight cut across it is a segment.

detailed.definition: A sector is the region enclosed by two radii and the arc between them. A segment is the region enclosed by a chord and the corresponding arc. The minor sector or segment is the smaller of the two parts.
detailed.key_idea: Every formula in the chapter is the whole-circle formula multiplied by θ/360. Once that is seen, only the area and circumference of a circle need to be remembered.
detailed.working_principle: Area of a segment = area of the sector − area of the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord. Choosing the right triangle formula for that step is where most marks are lost.
applications: Area swept by a clock hand or a windscreen wiper is a sector area.
Grazing area of an animal tied at the corner of a field is a sector.
Designs combining circles and squares are handled by adding and subtracting areas.

points: Area of segment = area of sector − area of the triangle.
For a 60° sector the triangle is equilateral, with area (√3/4)r².
Area of sector can also be written as ½ × arc length × r.
mistakes: Using θ/180 instead of θ/360 in the sector formulas.
Forgetting to subtract the triangle when the segment is required.
Using the diameter in place of the radius.
topics.memory_hook: 'Sector = slice of pizza; Segment = sector minus triangle.'
topics.advanced: In radian measure the formulas simplify to arc = rθ and sector area = ½r²θ, with no 360 anywhere. That simplification is the whole reason radians are the standard unit in higher mathematics.

formulas.name: Arc Length and Sector Area
formulas.formula: Arc = (θ/360)·2πr;  Sector area = (θ/360)·πr² = ½ × arc × r
formulas.variables: θ = central angle in degrees, r = radius.
formulas.when_to_use: For any sector, wiper, grazing or clock-hand problem.
formulas.shortcut: θ = 90° gives a quarter circle; θ = 180° gives a semicircle.

formulas.name: Area of a Segment
formulas.when_to_use: For the region between a chord and its arc.
formulas.common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract the triangular part.
formulas.shortcut: For θ = 60° the triangle is equilateral with area (√3/4)r².
